scope: Transport feasibility comparison, not an implemented child_process backend. Only ToolRpc.invokeAndAwait has experimental synchronous lowering; the async observer path is unchanged.

pressure.collection: JS sums bytes and checksum rather than retaining all output.

sync.failure: stream scheduling probe timed out: streams-pressure-sync

interpretation: The async reader/terminal path completes all five calls. The child is explicitly cancelled only after its output marker is observed, then the same owner successfully invokes another fresh sidecar.

The blocking terminal import completes small channels and binary echo, but cannot complete the 32 MiB output with JavaScript-owned readers. Its trace reaches 258 output-write host calls and no output finish before timeout; no panic or host-resource-exhausted terminal was observed.
Write host-call counts are attempts, not accepted bytes. The async pressure segment also includes the outer probe output; these are not isolated child host-call or oplog counts.

This is consistent with buffer backpressure while JS cannot continue reading. It does not establish an upstream defect: the existing tool contract explicitly requires concurrent reader/terminal progress.
nextGate: A sync call must collect bounded output outside the paused QuickJS runtime, preserving normal tool admission, journaled host attachment observations, cancellation and replay. Simply composing guest-visible host convenience functions inside another host call is not valid: completion delivery must remain a tail operation.
